Dark Matter is a horrible name. Basically, when light travels vast distances it is affected by the gravity of the celestial bodies it passes. This effect is known as 'lensing.' Gravity changes the path that the light would take if it were unimpeded.

Now, we generally have a pretty good model of what is supposed to happen. However, light is impacted more than it should be, given the known amount of matter. This effect, and whatever is causing it, is known as 'Dark Matter.'

We can't directly observe it, but we can see the effect that it has and infer it. We haven't a damned clue what is actually causing the effects. Anyone suggesting that they know, with any level of confidence, can be safely ignored as a charlatan and not a practitioner of the scientific method.

By the way, we are really, really good at predicting this. Over many millions of miles, we can predict the exact location, in both space and time, well enough to capture images of minute numbers of photons. Astronomers do so all the time.

This same effect was what helped prove Einstein's theory of General Relativity. After an eclipse, they were able to capture an image of a star while it was still behind Sol, our sun.
